title: Sultanate of Hobyo
capsule: The Sultanate of Hobyo (Sultanate of the Sons of Kenadid) was founded by Yusuf Ali Kenadid in the early 1880s on the central Somali coast, with its capital at Hobyo (Obbia), after he broke away from the Majeerteen Sultanate. Kenadid built a centralized state with a professional army and hereditary administrative structure controlling much of the central Somali coast and its immediate hinterland. In 1889 Kenadid signed a treaty making Hobyo an Italian protectorate, trading recognition and arms for formal protection; Italy progressively tightened its grip, and in 1925 the Italian colonial administration forcibly deposed Kenadid's son and successor, abolishing the sultanate as part of the pacification of Italian Somaliland. The dataset's terminal date of 1895 reflects the early protectorate phase when the sultanate retained substantive internal autonomy.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The sultanate's political history is documented in Italian colonial records and Somali oral tradition, but its precise territorial extent in the hinterland is poorly mapped and the coastal core is better attested than inland boundaries.
